freshservice_domain.description: AI-Triage v1.8.2 (see CHANGELOG.md for release notes). Your Freshservice domain, host only, no https. Example: yourcompany.freshservice.com

regex.host-only-error: Enter the domain only, no https:// prefix or trailing slash — e.g. yourcompany.freshservice.com

freshservice_api_key.description: API key used to post the private triage note. Uses the scoped service agent key (least-privilege: read tickets/Solutions, write private notes only).

ai_provider.description: Which AI service performs the triage. Choose 'anthropic' (Claude), 'openai' (ChatGPT), or 'copilot' (Microsoft Copilot via Azure OpenAI). Fill in the API key and fields for whichever one you pick — the other providers' fields are ignored.

anthropic_api_key.description: API key for the Anthropic Claude API (console.anthropic.com). Required only when AI Provider is 'anthropic'.

claude_model.description: Model ID used when AI Provider is 'anthropic'. Sonnet 5 is the default. Use claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 for the cheapest/fastest option.

openai_api_key.description: API key for the OpenAI API (platform.openai.com — note this is separate from a ChatGPT subscription and needs its own prepaid credit balance). Required only when AI Provider is 'openai'.

openai_model.description: Model ID used when AI Provider is 'openai'. gpt-5.6-terra balances cost and capability. Use gpt-5.6-luna for the cheapest option, or gpt-5.6-sol for the most capable.

openai_host.description: Host for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no https. Leave as api.openai.com unless you are pointing at a different OpenAI-compatible service.

copilot_api_key.description: API key for your Azure OpenAI resource (found in Azure portal → your resource → Keys and Endpoint). Required only when AI Provider is 'copilot'.

copilot_endpoint_host.description: Host for your Azure OpenAI resource, no https. Example: my-resource.openai.azure.com. Required only when AI Provider is 'copilot'.

copilot_deployment.description: The deployment name you configured in Azure OpenAI Studio (e.g. gpt-4o-prod). This is the name in the URL path — NOT the underlying model name. Required only when AI Provider is 'copilot'.

copilot_api_version.description: Azure OpenAI API version string. Defaults to 2025-01-01-preview. Only change if your deployment requires a different version.

copilot_model.display_name: Azure OpenAI Base Model (for cost reporting)
copilot_model.description: The underlying model your Azure deployment is based on, e.g. gpt-4o or gpt-4o-mini. Used only for cost estimation in the report — does not affect the API call. Leave blank to suppress cost tracking.

output_budget.description: Cap on the triage note length (max output tokens). Lower keeps latency well under the execution cap.

enable_web_search.description: When enabled, the AI may search the web to ground triage notes with current, cited sources. Supported on both providers. WARNING: enabling web search increases per-ticket AI cost — roughly $0.01 per search plus extra tokens. Leave unchecked to disable.

web_search_max_uses.description: Upper bound on web searches per ticket (only applies when web search is enabled, and only enforceable on the Anthropic provider). Keeps cost and latency bounded under the execution cap.

enable_deflection.description: When enabled, known recurring/automated ticket types (admin consent, quarantine release, quarterly maintenance, Box/OneDrive links, employee termination) get a prewritten internal note that links the KB to follow and names the canned response to use — skipping the AI call entirely. Uncheck to send every ticket through AI triage.

poc_group_id.description: OPTIONAL PoC safety gate. If set, only tickets in this group are triaged; all others are skipped. Enter 0 to disable this gate and triage every new ticket. Use during PoC in the main environment to limit blast radius.

poc_workspace_id.description: OPTIONAL PoC safety gate. If set, only tickets in this workspace are triaged; all others are skipped. Enter 0 to disable this gate. Combine with PoC Group ID for a narrower gate, or use alone to cover an entire workspace (e.g. IT — workspace 2).
